hero.title: Why Our Funding Is Fit-for-Purpose
hero.summary: Strong growth is grounded in trust. The funding model prioritizes community leadership, flexible support, and long-term institutional strengthening.

modules.title: Partner Profile and Accountability Model
modules.summary: Tenure Facility supports Indigenous, Afro-descendant, and local community organizations, with most partner organizations directly accountable to their membership and territories.

columns.heading: Community-rooted partners
paragraphs: Partners include Indigenous NGOs, territorial funds, and community organizations operating at local and national levels across the regions where projects are active.
Many are grassroots, member-based organizations formed by communities to represent their interests and channel finance to local priorities.

columns.heading: Working with allied organizations
paragraphs: Where direct community organizations cannot access larger international grants, the model also works through allied organizations that support implementation while remaining accountable to community-defined outcomes.
A core operating principle is that organization achievements are attributed to partner organizations unless stated otherwise.

modules.title: A Fit-for-Purpose Funding Approach
modules.summary: The finance model adapts to partner context while preserving accountability, FPIC principles, and local decision-making power.

columns.heading: Working with partner realities
paragraphs: Capacity levels vary between partners and regions. Funding pathways are tailored to local context so organizations can absorb support without distorting community priorities.
The approach combines flexible grant agreements, simplified systems, and practical compliance support to meet both donor and partner needs.

columns.heading: Building long-term legitimacy
paragraphs: Projects are rooted in Free, Prior and Informed Consent consultations, with decisions led by communities and partner organizations.
The objective is durable governance, stronger organizations, and greater financial autonomy over time.

modules.title: Funding
modules.summary: As geopolitical uncertainty increases, community-led finance remains a practical route to protect rights, ecosystems, and democratic participation.

columns.heading: Budget and funding sources
paragraphs: The 2024 budget was just under USD 40 million and was supported by two dozen funders, with three new funders joining in 2024.
Large commitments include multi-year support for the Amazon Catalyst, alongside diversified philanthropic and public finance streams.

columns.heading: Institutional readiness
paragraphs: Operational systems were strengthened in 2024 through consolidated project tracking, updated procurement policy, improved reporting workflows, and team training.
These upgrades support scale while maintaining trust-based relationships and mission alignment.

quote.text: In times of growing global uncertainty, the role of civil society organisations is more vital than ever.
